title: Structure à l'infini des Mg,ν [pages 1 à 90, dont table des matières] : notes manuscrites (s.d.).

deep.reconstruction:
Context: Grothendieck is formalizing the 'structure at infinity' of the moduli spaces M_{g,ν}. This means the stratification of the boundary (the Deligne–Mumford divisor, a normal-crossings divisor with self-intersections) by codimension d, i.e. by the number of nodes. On the previous page he introduces a 'category object' D in analytic spaces (or stacks):
- D_* is the space of objects, with a codimension function c: D_* → N, so D_* = ∐_d D_d.
- D_** is the space of arrows, split as ∐ D_{d,d'} by the codimensions of source and target.
- Axioms (174): (a) arrows only go from codim d to codim d' ≤ d; (b) an arrow between objects of equal codimension is an identity; (c) a condition on the source map, presumably étale/finite.

This page continues axiom (c). The source map restricted over D_d is σ_d: D_{d,*} := ∐_{d'} D_{d,d'} = σ^{-1}(D_d) → D_d.
- It is a finite étale 'multiplicial' covering of D_d.
- It carries a relative order: arrows with a given source are ordered by factorizability (x→z ≤ x→y if x→y factors through z). It also carries a 'cardinal' function giving d'.
- As an ordered covering with cardinality function it is the twisted form of the constant family 𝒫(I_d)° (the power set of a d-element set I_d, ordered by inclusion, graded by cardinality).
- Hence it amounts to an S_d-principal covering D_d^! of D_d (the frame of the d local branches/nodes), and D_{d,d'} = D_d^! ×^{S_d} {subsets of I_d of cardinality d'}.

Model case: a normal-crossings divisor, with D_d = the normalization of the closed d-fold locus. Points of D_d are a point together with d branches, and arrows choose a subset of d' of these branches. In M_{g,ν}, 'branches' are nodes and an arrow 'forgets', i.e. smooths, the complementary nodes.

Grothendieck then observes that D_d^! alone recovers the D_{d,d'} but not the whole category. One must also give the target maps b: D_{d,d'} → D_{d'}, and the composition maps D_{d,d'} ×_{D_{d'}} D_{d',d''} → D_{d,d''}. The reason is that it is unclear from the hypotheses so far whether D_{d,d''} → D_d × D_{d''} is a monomorphism, i.e. whether arrows are determined by source and target. He suggests this might follow from (c).

The next page resolves the issue differently. It gives (D_d), the torsors D_d^!, the maps b, and cartesian squares (175) identifying the pullback of D_{d'}^! with the tautological S_{d'}-torsor of D_{d,d'}. From these, D_{d,d',d''} and the composition maps are derived. The purpose is a purely combinatorial-analytic description of the boundary stratification of \bar M_{g,ν}, as input to studying tubular neighbourhoods 'at infinity' and the Teichmüller tower.
errors: The hoped-for statement that D_{d,d''} → D_d × D_{d''} is a monomorphism ('arrows determined by source and target') fails in the intended stacky setting of \bar M_{g,ν}. A stable curve can have automorphisms permuting its nodes, so distinct subsets of nodes, i.e. distinct arrows, can share source and target. Equivalently, the map of stacks is not fully faithful. So the monomorphism cannot follow from a covering axiom like (c) alone. It does hold for a normal-crossings divisor on a scheme (no automorphisms), where distinct branch-subsets give distinct points of the normalized stratum. Grothendieck's switch on the next page to giving b and the cartesian squares (175) explicitly sidesteps exactly this issue, which suggests he recognized the problem.
Minor: the direction of the 'factorizability' order versus inclusion of branch subsets is not made explicit, but either convention is consistent.

ideas.what: Encoding the boundary stratification of a (self-intersecting) normal-crossings divisor / of \bar M_{g,ν} as a category object in analytic spaces. Objects are strata points graded by codimension; arrows go from deeper to shallower strata, with identity-only arrows in equal codimension.
ideas.modern_name: exit-path / stratification category; category of stable graphs (as a category internal to stacks); boundary complex
ideas.usually_credited_to: MacPherson (exit paths), Treumann (2009) and Lurie (HA, appendix A) for exit-path ∞-categories; Getzler–Kapranov (1998) for modular operads / stable-graph category; Abramovich–Caporaso–Payne and Chan–Galatius–Payne for the boundary complex as a generalized cone complex
ideas.where_published: Esquisse d'un programme discusses the 'structure à l'infini' / boundary of M_{g,ν} and the Teichmüller tower informally; this categorical formalism is not given there as far as I know

ideas.what: The source-fibre over D_d is a finite étale covering whose fibres are power sets ordered by inclusion with a cardinality grading. It is the twist of 𝒫(I_d) by an S_d-torsor D_d^! (orderings of branches/nodes), and the D_{d,d'} are associated bundles D_d^! ×^{S_d} Sub_{d'}(I_d).
ideas.modern_name: torsor of orderings of local branches; orientation local system ε^d; the 'cubical/Boolean' local model of a log structure with monoid N^d
ideas.usually_credited_to: Deligne (Théorie de Hodge II, 1971: normalizations of d-fold intersections and orientation sheaves); later log geometry (K. Kato, Fontaine–Illusie, ~1988–89)

ideas.what: Recognition that the torsors D_d^! do not determine the category. One needs target maps and composition, and the arrows-determined-by-endpoints property is non-automatic.
ideas.modern_name: non-posetal (EI-type) stratification categories, as for orbifold/stack stratifications
ideas.usually_credited_to: implicit in work on exit-path categories of stacks and on the stable-graph category with automorphisms

missed.claim: Grothendieck sets up the boundary of \bar M_{g,ν} as an internal category in analytic spaces/stacks, graded by codimension. Arrows from codim d are classified by the Boolean lattice of node-subsets, twisted by the S_d-torsor of node-orderings. This is essentially a pre-formulation of the category of stable graphs / exit-path category of the DM stratification as a geometric (not just combinatorial) object. It anticipates Getzler–Kapranov-style and tropical (Abramovich–Caporaso–Payne, Chan–Galatius–Payne) descriptions of the boundary complex, but packaged as a category internal to the strata themselves.
missed.quote: qui fait de D_{d,*} un rev. multiplicial sur D_d, relativement ordonné (par la relation de factorisabilité des flèches de source donnée)
missed.why_it_might_matter_today: It provides an early, geometric version of a framework now used to compute boundary complexes and weight-zero cohomology of M_{g,n}. Mainly of historical interest; the mathematics itself is now standard.

deep.surprise_reason: A careful, early categorical formalization of the normal-crossings boundary stratification of \bar M_{g,ν}, with the S_d-torsor reconstruction of the Boolean fibres. It is historically interesting as a precursor of exit-path and stable-graph categories, but the content (branch-ordering torsors, power-set fibres) is standard by Deligne's Hodge II and later work. The open question he raises has a negative answer in the stacky case.
transcription_corrections: 'rev. multiplique' is likely 'rev. multiplicial' (cf. 'ensembles ordonnés multipliciaux' a few lines below).
'cet rev. correspondant à E [?]' is more likely '(est le rev. correspondant à ...)' leading into '𝒫(I_d)^*_{D_d}'. The script letter before (I_d) is 𝒫 (power set), not ℰ.
'principal de groupe G_d': the script letter is likely 𝔖_d (symmetric group), consistent with the next page.
'D_{d^*,d'} × D_{d',d''} → D_{d^*,d''}' should read D_{d,d'} ×_{D_{d'}} D_{d',d''} → D_{d,d''}; the asterisk-like mark is a stray stroke.
'avec les seules hyp. faites jusqu'ici : prismes' is uncertain; possibly 'précisées' or a reference to a hypothesis label, rather than 'prismes'.
'Cela redonne dans un sens D_d^!': the exclamation mark is the superscript of D_d^! (the S_d-torsor), as on the next page.
'sont mono ?, i.e. que' is a correct reading.
